Consult Summary:
- Female patient with six days of dysuria, suprapubic/lower abdominal pain, and blood in urine, without fever; exam planned as empirical urinary tract infection treatment with a three-day antibiotic course, hydration, and supportive measures; return or escalation advised if symptoms worsen or recur.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Burning/pain with urination for six days; unpleasant smell of urine; accompanying lower abdominal pain (midline) rated 7/10; pain is intermittent; able to pass urine with some symptoms.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began six days ago and have persisted; pain fluctuates; no fever.
- Associated symptoms: Blood in urine (spotting) for six days; appetite and hydration generally good; no flank/loin pain; no vaginal discharge reported; regular menstrual periods; no weight loss reported.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: None specified.
- Review of systems: No fever; no back/loin pain; no weight loss; able to eat/drink; no high-temperature episodes.
- Relevant negatives: No fever, no loin pain, no abdominal/back imaging findings documented.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) noted; other medical history denied in some parts of the conversation (conflict noted in PMH).
- Medications: Mebeverine, 200 mg, three times daily; route not documented.
- Allergies: Clindamycin.
- Social history: Lives with friends; works as a support worker; drinks alcohol occasionally (about one glass of wine per week); non-smoker.
- Family history: Not reported.
- Time line: Six days of symptoms continuing; no prior similar episodes documented.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
- No other medical problems documented consistently (note potential conflict below).
- Medications: Mebeverine 200 mg, three times daily; route not documented.
- Allergies: Clindamycin.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with friends.
- Occupation: Support worker.
- Alcohol: Occasional; approximately one glass of wine per week.
- Smoking: No.

Family History:

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not provided.
- Examination findings: Not provided.

Investigations:
- Urine testing: Not performed at this visit; plan is to treat empirically for presumed UTI.
- Additional tests: Not documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute urinary tract infection (probable cystitis) with dysuria, midline lower abdominal pain, and gross/trace hematuria.
  - Plan:
    - Empiric antibiotic therapy for 3 days; prescription sent to patient’s requested pharmacy (Knightsbridge Practice) with pick-up expected within about an hour.
    - Advise high fluid intake: 2.5–3 liters per day.
    - Recommend cranberry juice as supportive measure.
    - Recommend urine-acidity increasing sachets (over-the-counter) to be taken as advised.
    - Provide home temperature monitoring guidance; obtain a thermometer from the pharmacy and check temperature if fever develops.
    - Return for reassessment or if symptoms worsen, if high fever develops, if pain worsens or persists despite treatment, or if there is any difficulty passing urine.
    - If symptoms recur or become a common problem, reconsider diagnosis and management.
    - Note: Allergy to Clindamycin documented; antibiotic choice will avoid this agent.
    - Follow-up instructions: If better, no need to call after finishing antibiotic course; if worse or not resolving, contact for further evaluation.
- Issue 2: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) history.
  - Plan:
    - Continue current management with Mebeverine; no changes documented.
- Issue 3: Medication allergy safety.
  - Plan:
    - Document Clindamycin allergy; ensure antibiotic selection is appropriate to avoid this agent.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No documented vitals (BP, HR, temp) at visit.
  - No explicit urine analysis or culture results (not performed per plan).
  - No explicit imaging or laboratory results.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Inconsistent PMH: patient stated “no medical problems” when asked previously, but later reports IBS. Conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall clear; occasional repetition and minor conversational awkwardness, but information is comprehensible. No major inaudible segments noted.

Notes:
- The antibiotic name is not specified in the transcript; plan notes empirical therapy with avoidance of Clindamycin due to allergy.
- A pharmacy has been requested for Knightsbridge Practice; pickup anticipated around lunchtime.
